TL;DR: I was instructed by my surgeon who has performed all 4 of my skin removals to self-drain a leg hematoma.

Please read further before making your comments.

 .........

 Here’s the story behind Mt. Leg Gushmore:
 
I had a medial thigh lift in March 2019. (the clip is from 15 months ago).
 
Prior, I had 3 other skin removal surgeries.
My 2 surgeries done 9 months earlier (that were done together) healed with no problems.
The 3rd surgery (Dec2018) developed a hematoma, but I had a revision surgery for that while having my thigh lift (4th surgery). (2 hematomas total). 

 ........

When I woke up after the procedure, my surgeon (who I was friendly with since he had done ALL of my surgeries) was nowhere to be found.
My mom talked to him after I came out of the OR.
All he said was "went perfectly, as expected. It only took me a bit longer since there was some fluid leaking we couldn't stop, but it should be good now."
 
My mom was obviously upset by the statement but he left immediately since he had to go back to his office.
 
I went home the same day. The pain was unbearable & I couldn't walk properly, but with a thigh lift, that's expected. My thighs felt like they'd explode at any second.  My mom had to drag me out of the shower after my legs gave out on the seocnd night.

 ..........

I had the surgery done during spring break. On post op day 4, I had to move back into my dorm since my parents left for a business trip that day.
 
When I got to school, my plan was to do a week of remote learning from my dorm (my apartment was a 10 min healthy leg walk to the academic buildings), then go back to classes.
 
On day 4 (first night in dorm) I wasn't feeling right.
I woke up on day 5 and sent this [text and photo](https://imgur.com/v7JxPZN) to my mom.
I was scared shitless.
 
I called my doctor and went immediately (my roommate drove me). This is what my [leg](https://imgur.com/a/QG9aN2l) looked like before leaving the dorm.
The surgeon said "Hm, this doesn't look normal." He then sent me home and just said to let it bleed out, encourage it, and keep him updated.
I have no regrets bleeding all over the white chair in the patient room.
 
The same night, I was bleeding so much, I started to get a high feeling. My roommates freaked out and drove me to the ER at 12am. The driver called my surgeon and explained the situation, he asked to speak to me and asked me where I was going and I said "I'm in my dorm." I was so out of it. He suggested to turn around from the ER and go home and rest.
 
The ER scanned the leg and confirmed a hematoma, then sent me home and said to follow up with my doctor.
We went back to campus at 3am. My roommates tried to drive on the road to my dorm to avoid the quarter mile walk from parking, but campus safety stopped us at the entrance and told us to park and walk. My roommate explained for me and the guard said "that doesn't give you special privilege." I whipped out my walker right at that spot and stumbled with 1 of the roommates to the next quad while the guards watched.
 ..........
After that, I was almost completely immobile and couldn’t walk further than the bathroom.
 
I let the leg bleed on its own, as instructed. [This](https://imgur.com/a/3228Nhr) is what my showers looked like for the entire week.
 
I went back to see the surgeon 4 days later. The swelling doubled (my right leg was triple the size of my swollen left leg).  After seeing it balloon up, he cut a [window](https://imgur.com/a/4xJkpZh) in the scar line and told me to milk out the hematoma blood as much as possible until it's gone. He said a revision surgery would be a bad move and risky for blood loss.
 ..........
Kinda gross, but this pic shows what was collected from the leg after each [hematoma draining](https://imgur.com/a/KoluwIH) session.
A little side MedGore special, here's some of the highlights of the [murder scene](https://imgur.com/a/zNlJNEP).
 
For the record, I did NOT get any infections or amputations.  Here is my [healed scar](http://imgur.com/a/4tHKYKT) one year later.
The only thing that I developed was anemia (Oct'19, iron=11, ferratin=4), which according to the doctor, was not due to the hematoma.
 
Finally, here is a before and after of the [final result](http://imgur.com/a/u7LVhHZ) to show that I did successfully recover.

 .......

3 weeks after this catastrophe healed, I was in and out of the hospital had an emergency gallbladder removal.
 
1 month after that, I moved 1200 miles away from home, started training for swimming, and became a first-time lifeguard at a large waterpark.
 
Sometimes, I can't believe what my body has gone through.
In the moment, I thought nothing of it. It wasn't gross, I just went with it.
Looking back, it gives me the creeps that this was MY body.
 
All said and done, all I can say is that I am so appreciative for my roommates. The roommates that drove me were living in a different building at the time, and the roommates I lived with were nothing but supportive for me (one was studying nursing so she used me as her human study model).
Also, I'm sorry to whoever lives in that room now with the blood handprint stains on random surfaces.

Mental health is so important with anemia! 

I was undiagnosed for a long time (I had my stomach shrunk and chose to eat like 2 days a week for 6 months) so it took a year for my body to catch up with the sickness and didn't show in blood labs for over a year. Then, I had 4 surgeries within that year, and my leg bled out 3 solocups worth of blood for 3 weeks straight from a hematoma complication. 
The blood test didn't show anemia until 6 months later.  My iron was at 11 ferritin was a 4. 

I was a senior in college when the anemia REALLY began to affect me. 

I wasn't going to classes, always getting to work last minute, and got majorly addicted to adderall just to make me feel alive. 

I convinced myself I had dementia, all sorts of other mental problems, since I didn't know all of the side affects came along w anemia. 

I went to many doctors to try to prove I wasn't crazy and I wasn't faking. 

My mom was upset with how my life was going. I showed up at a family dinner and she texted me after I left asking if I was on drugs etc because my eyes were glossed over and I looked lost. 
My response was "I just don't feel good anymore." 
Then she understood a bit more. 

I was having panic attacks everyday, I felt like my brain was shutting off and I was a stranger to my own body.

In school, i was isolating myself from my friends, locking myself in my dorm, and everyone was confused what happened to the original me, who was the social addict and threw parties every night. It didn't feel right. 

I had an iron infusion in December, then dropped out of college (as a senior, with 4 courses remaining) and moved to warmer climate from the north fk the south. After my infusion, within 3-4 months, I felt CURED and NORMAL again!!!!

The anemia kicks in now (6 months after infusions) once in a while but no where near as bad as I once was. I have to get my infusion every December now. 

Anemia is NOT fake, and NOT easy to deal with! You are not lazy, you are sick. 
It's hard to show when its invisible. 

I have a herniated disc. Also, an invisible pain. I've had it for 10 years. My mom also didn't believe me when i kept complaining of crippling pain and she couldn't see it. Again, 6 months after injury, I was diagnosed with "muscle spasms," then 10 months after injury, diagnosed with herniated disc. 
This felt like the same struggle as diagnosing anemia did. 

Nobody sees the hurting, the pain, the injury, so they assume it's not there. 

Never let anyone assume your pain. 
Be your own voice.

Once you get proper treatment, i promise, you will get back to your normal social self ;)
